questions.question: ______ is the first state in India which has made roof top rainwater harvesting structure compulsory to all the houses across the state.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Tamil Nadu.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu** is the **first state in India** which has made **roof top rainwater harvesting **structure compulsory to all the **houses** across the state.
 
• The state government has made it** mandatory **for all buildings with a **minimum built-up area of 100 square meters** to install a rainwater harvesting system.
 
• The government has also** provided subsidies** to encourage households to adopt this** eco-friendly measure.**
 
• This initiative has helped in** conserving water **and **recharging groundwater** levels in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haryana **has also made rainwater harvesting mandatory for all buildings with a **roof area **of more than **100 square meters.**
 
• **West Bengal **has launched a scheme for **rainwater harvesting** in **rural areas**.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has launched a program called **"Sujalam Sufalam" **to promote **water conservation** and **rainwater harvesting** in the state.

questions.question: In ______ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1940.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The resolution demanding **"Independent States"** for **Muslims** was passed on **23rd March 1940** in **Lahore **at the** All-India Muslim League's annual session.**
 
• The resolution was moved by **Fazlul Huq,** the Chief Minister of Bengal, and seconded by **Chaudhary Khaliquzzaman**, a prominent Muslim League leader.
 
• The resolution stated that the areas in which the Muslims were **numerically in a majority** as in the north-western and **eastern zones of India** should be grouped to constitute **"independent states".**
 
• This resolution is famously known as the **Lahore Resolution or the Pakistan Resolution**, which eventually led to the **creation of Pakistan in 1947.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, **1942: In 1942, the** Quit India Movemen**t was launched by** Mahatma Gandhi** against British rule in India.
 
• **Option 2**, 1943: In 1943, the **Bengal Famine **occurred, which resulted in the **deaths** of millions of people due to starvation and disease.
 
• **Option 4,** 1938: In 1938, the Muslim League passed the **"Fourteen Points" resolution, **which demanded **separate electorates **for **Muslims,** **reservation of seats** in the **legislatures, **and other political rights for the Muslim community in India.

• The Act makes the practice of triple talaq a **cognizable and non-bailable offence**, punishable with **imprisonment **for up to **three years** and a **fine.**
 
• The Act also provides for the** payment of subsistence allowance **to married Muslim women and their **dependent children** in case of triple talaq.

• **Option 4, Protection of Women Act,** is also not a specific law and there is no such Act by this name in India.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement with respect to Earth.

options.text: The diameter of the equator increases till the poles.
The radius of earth increases from the poles to the equator.
The diameter of earth decreases from the poles to the equator.
The radius of earth decreases from the poles to the equator.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The radius of earth increases from the poles to the equator.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct option is** option 2,** which states that the radius of the Earth **increases** from the poles to the equator.
 
• This is due to the fact that the Earth is** not a perfect sphere, **but rather an oblate spheroid, which means that it is **slightly flattened** at the **poles** and **bulges** at the **equator.**
 
• The** equatorial diameter of the Earth** is about **12,742 km, **while its** polar diameter** is about **12,714 km.**
 
• This means that the** distance **from the **center of the Earth** to the **equator** is **slightly longer** than the distance from the center to the poles, resulting in a **larger radius at the equator.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1,** which states that the diameter of the equator increases till the poles, is **incorrect** as it is the opposite of the correct statement.
 
• **Option 3,** which states that the diameter of the Earth decreases from the poles to the equator, is also** incorrect** as it is the opposite of the correct statement.
 
• **Option 4,** which states that the radius of the Earth decreases from the poles to the equator, is also** incorrect** as it is the opposite of the correct statement.
 
• Hence, the **statement 2** is** correct **as it explains the shape of the Earth and how it affects the radius at different points.

questions.question: Which Sub-Section of Fundamental Duties talks about the duty to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired our national struggle for freedom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sub-Section b.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sub-Section b **of Fundamental Duties talks about the duty to** cherish and follow the noble ideals** that inspired our** national struggle** for freedom.
 
• This sub-section is mentioned under **Article 51A **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Fundamental Duties **were added to the Indian Constitution in **1976** by the **42nd Amendment Act.**
 
• The objective of Fundamental Duties is to promote the **spirit of patriotism **and to uphold the **dignity of the nation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sub-Section d **talks about the duty to** defend the country **and **render national service** when required.
 
• **Sub-Section c** talks about the duty to uphold and protect the** sovereignty, unity, and integrity **of India.
 
• **Sub-Section a** talks about the duty to **abide by the Constitution** and respect its** ideals and institutions.**
 
• Hence, the **correct** answer is option 1, i.e., Sub-Section b.

questions.question: __________ are foreign currency assets held by the central banks of countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Foreign exchange Reserves.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct answer** is **option 2**, foreign exchange reserves are **foreign currency** assets held by **central banks.**
 
• Foreign exchange reserves are an important tool for central banks to manage their **country's currency **and** maintain stability** in the foreign **exchange market.**
 
• These reserves are usually held in the form of **foreign currencies, government bonds, and gold.**
 
• They can be used to intervene in the market by** buying or selling currencies** to influence their value or to **provide liquidity** to banks during times of **financial stress.**
 
• Countries with large foreign exchange reserves are often seen as **more stable and attractive** to investors, as they have the ability to weather **economic shocks **and maintain the** value of their currency.**
 
• **Rate exchange, credit control, and local exchange** are not equivalent to foreign exchange reserves and do not refer to the same concept.
 
• Hence, options 1, 3, and 4 are** incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rate exchange** refers to the rate at which** one currency** can be* ***exchanged f**or another.

 
 
• It is determined by the foreign exchange market and influenced by various factors such as **economic conditions and political events.**
 
 
 
• **Credit control** refers to the measures taken by a** central bank **to regulate the **availability and cost of credit **in the economy.
 
 
• This includes setting **interest rates **and** reserve requirements** for banks.
 
 
 
• Local exchange refers to the **exchange of one currency** for another within a **specific country or region.**

questions.question: In Cricket, what is the distance between two wickets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22 yards.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **distance between two wickets** in cricket is** 22 yards **or **20.12 meters.**
 
• The distance is measured from the** center of both the wickets.**
 
• The two wickets are placed at a** distance of 1.22 meters** or **4 feet** and **1 inch **from each other.
 
• The wickets are made of **three wooden stumps** with** two wooden bails **placed on top of them.
 
• Option 2, 3, and 4 are** incorrect** as the distance between two wickets is 22 yards and not any of the other options mentioned.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The game is played between **two teams**, each consisting of **11 players.**
 
• The objective of the game is to score as many runs as possible while also dismissing the opposition team's batsmen.
 
• The game is played on a** circular or oval-shaped field** with a rectangular 22-yard-long pitch in the center.

questions.question: Which among the following festivals is also known as the festival of winter season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chakan Gaan-Ngai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chakan Gaan-Ngai **is the festival of the **Zeliangrong tribe** of** Manipur and Nagaland,** which is celebrated during the** winter season.**
 
• The festival is also known as the** festival of lights** as people light up their homes with** lamps and candles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moatsu** is a festival of the **Ao tribe of Nagaland**, which is celebrated in the **month of May** to mark the end of the** sowing season.**
 
• **Wangala **is a harvest festival of the **Garo tribe of Meghalaya**, which is celebrated in the **month of November** to thank the gods for a bountiful **harvest.**
 
• **Chapchar Kut **is a spring festival of the** Mizos of Mizoram,** which is celebrated in the** month of March** to welcome the** spring season.**
 
• Hence, the **correct** answer is **option 2**, Chakan Gaan-Ngai, which is the festival of the winter season.

questions.question: The second phase of green revolution in India existed from ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mid-1970s to mid-1980s.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** second phase** of the green revolution in India existed from **mid-1970s to mid-1980s. **
 
• It was characterized by the introduction of **high-yielding varieties of seeds**, increased use of **fertilizers**, and improved** irrigation facilities.**
 
• The objective was to increase** agricultural productivity** and ensure** food security** in the country.
 
• The second phase was successful in increasing **food production** and reducing the **dependence on food imports.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The mid-1950s to mid-1960s was the** first phase** of the green revolution in India, which focused on the introduction of **new crop varieties** and **modern agricultural techniques.**
 
• **Option 2:** The mid-1960s to mid-1970s was a** transitional phase** between the first and second phase of the green revolution in India.
 
• **Option 4:** The mid-1980s to mid-1990s saw the introduction of **new agricultural policies,** such as **liberalization and privatization, **which aimed to **increase efficiency** and **reduce government intervention** in the **agricultural sector.**

questions.question: What is a group of industries that tend to come together to make use of the advantages offered by the urban centers known as ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**agglomeration economies.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agglomeration economies** refer to the benefits that arise from the** clustering of industries **in **urban centers**. These benefits include:

 
 
• **Economies of scale:** Firms can **share infrastructure and resources, **reducing costs and increasing efficiency.
 
• **Access to skilled labor:** A concentration of industries in one area can attract a** skilled workforce, **making it easier for firms to find and hire qualified employees. 
 
• **Innovation**: Proximity to other firms can lead to knowledge **spillovers and collaboration,** fostering innovation and growth.
 
• **Reduced transportation costs**: By locating near other firms and suppliers, firms can reduce transportation costs and increase speed of delivery.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rural economies** refer to economies that are based on** agriculture and natural resources.**
 
• **Amalgamation economies** refer to the benefits that arise from the **consolidation of firms** in a particular industry.
 
• **Urban economies **refer to the** overall economic activit**y and growth of urban areas.

questions.question: In India, the Executive power of the state is vested in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** is the **head of the state **and holds the **executive power** in India.
 
• The **Council of Ministers** is a body of advisors to the Governor, who assist in the exercise of **executive powers.**
 
• The **Chief Justice of High Court** is a** judicial **authority and **does not hold** executive powers.
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the** elected governmen**t in a state and exercises **executive powers **within the state, but not at the **national level.**
 
• The Governor is** appointed **by the **President of India** and holds office for a term of **five years,** unless removed earlier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Council of Ministers: **The Council of Ministers is a **body of advisors** to the Governor, led by the **Chief Minister.**

 
 
• It is responsible for the **administration of the state **and **advises** the Governor on matters related to governance.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of High Court:** The Chief Justice of High Court is the **head of the judiciary** in a state and is responsible for the** administration of justice** in the state.
 
• **Chief Minister**: The Chief Minister is the **head of the elected government **in a state and is responsible for the administration of the state.
 
 
• The Chief Minister is appointed by the** Governor **and **holds office **during the pleasure of the Governor.
 
 
 
• **Executive Power:** The executive power of the state refers to the power to **enforce laws and administer the government**.
 
 
• It is vested in the** Governor** in India.
